transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
My doctor sent me because my weight’s gotten so low and everyone’s making a big fuss about it. But honestly, I feel like being this light helps me keep up at the shop. I don’t feel slowed down.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes. If I eat something heavy, or the kinds of foods we used to make for holidays, I worry right away that I’m going to gain weight and lose the control I’ve worked hard to keep.
When you look at your body, do you see yourself as overweight?
I’m not sure I’d say overweight. I just see things on myself that I feel should be smaller, and it’s hard not to focus on that.
Have your menstrual periods stopped?
I’m not sure what you mean—could you explain?
Have your menstrual periods stopped?
I’m not really sure. What do you mean by stopped?
When was your last menstrual period?
I honestly couldn’t tell you. I haven’t been keeping track of it.
Have you gone at least three months without having a period?
I really don’t know. I haven’t been paying attention to whether it’s been that long.
Are you deliberately eating less in order to keep your weight down?
Yes. On days I’m in the workshop, I usually just have tea and maybe a few bites of something. Stopping for a proper meal feels unnecessary, and it sort of throws off the control I have over the day.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
I’m not sure what you mean—like intentionally making myself sick?
Yes—have you ever made yourself vomit on purpose after eating?
I’m not sure. I don’t really know what would count as doing it on purpose.
After you eat, have you ever put your fingers or anything else in your mouth to make yourself throw up?
I don’t know… I mean, I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Have you ever made yourself throw up on purpose to keep from gaining weight?
I… I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really connected it to keeping from gaining weight.
After eating, have you ever made yourself throw up on purpose?
I’m honestly not sure how to answer that. I haven’t really thought of it as something I was doing on purpose.
What is your current weight?
My weight has gotten pretty low—that’s why my doctor sent me here. People are making a big fuss about it, but I feel like being lighter helps me keep up at the shop and not get slowed down.
Did you lose this weight on purpose?

I suppose so, yes. On days I’m in the workshop, I usually just have tea and maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping for a proper meal feels unnecessary, and it throws off the control I have over the day.
Has any doctor told you that you are malnourished?
My husband and the apprentices say I’m too thin, but I don’t see it that way. I’m fine. I think they’re mistaking discipline for being sick.
What is your current weight?
It’s dropped low enough that my doctor sent me here. Everyone keeps making a fuss, but I feel all right—I’m lighter, and that helps me keep up at the shop.
How much do you weigh right now?
I don’t know the exact number right now. It’s low enough that my doctor sent me here, though. Everyone’s making a fuss about it, but I honestly feel like being lighter helps me keep up at the shop.
Do you believe your current weight is too low?
No, I don’t think it’s too low. My husband and the apprentices say I look thin, but I think they’re confusing discipline with being sick. I’m fine.
What is your height?
I’m not sure of my exact height. It hasn’t really changed, obviously—I’m about average, I think.
